thread.title: Manoj Mohanan appointed Duke vice provost for interdisciplinary programs
thread.title_full: Manoj Mohanan appointed Duke vice provost for interdisciplinary programs

author: Seyun Park
title: Manoj Mohanan appointed Duke vice provost for interdisciplinary programs
text:
Manoj Mohanan was named vice provost for interdisciplinary programs this week in an announcement released by Provost Alec Gallimore’s office. Currently interim dean of the Sanford School of Public Policy, he will transition into the new role July 1.
Reporting to Gallimore, Mohanan will oversee the Office of Interdisciplinary Programs which includes the University’s 11 institutes, initiatives and centers, as well as Bass Connections and DukeEngage.
The Office of Interdisciplinary Programs provides funding, oversight and facilitation to interdisciplinary units across the University. Through its various initiatives, the office reaches over half of all undergraduate students.
“Duke has been my intellectual home for 17 years, and I have benefited enormously from the interdisciplinary environment built by previous generations of Duke faculty and leaders,” Mohanan said. “I am excited to work with colleagues across our schools, institutes, centers and initiatives to steward and extend interdisciplinary approaches.”
Mohanan replaces Senior Vice Provost Ed Balleisen, who was appointed as provost and executive vice president of academic affairs at George Washington University. Balleisen has served as the vice provost for interdisciplinary programs and initiatives since 2015.
An internal search committee led by Lisa Gennetian, Pritzker professor at the Sanford School, selected Mohanan from a pool of multiple candidates.
“Mohanan distinguished himself throughout the search with his intellectual breadth, collaborative leadership and compelling vision for strengthening Duke’s interdisciplinary ecosystem,” Gennetian said. “[He] stood out for his ability to bring people and ideas together across disciplines and sectors.”
Mohanan will also serve as an ex officio member on the provost’s Interdisciplinary Strategy Council, which includes faculty representation from all nine University schools and advises the provost on interdisciplinary scholarship and programs.
Currently the Creed C. Black professor of Public Policy, Monahan is an alumnus of the University of Mumbai in India, where he earned his Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery, and Harvard University, where he earned a Master of Science in Public Health and a doctorate in health policy. As a professor and researcher, he has focused on applied microeconomics, specifically on health and healthcare in developing countries.
He joined Sanford’s faculty in 2011 and later served as a senior associate dean for faculty and research. He also holds appointments in economics and global health. In 2024, he was appointed interim dean of Sanford following then-Dean Judith Kelley’s decision to step down after a six-year term.
As interim dean, Mohanan guided Sanford through the University’s cost-cutting campaign, which included voluntary buyout and retirement incentives for many staff and faculty members. The school’s Center for International Development was hit particularly hard and forced to pause activity due to federal funding cuts, leaving just one full-time faculty member by May 2026. During Mohanan’s tenure, Sanford also launched a new technology policy minor that lies at the intersection of technology, governance and society.
He will be succeeded by JR DeShazo, who most recently served as the dean of the Lyndon B. Johnson School of Public Affairs at the University of Texas at Austin.
